faces.f: At the market, no one heeded Hilda's frantic mooing. The fae curse was turning out even worse than she had feared.
"Humans are so forgetful. Every page I steal becomes a secret they can't remember."
She yearned to walk on dry land so she might take her vengeance there.
It was built by the Witch of Lochmere. Most of the wishes it grants are its own.
"My secret ingredient? Well, I can't tell you that. But here's a hint. It's not love."

"Taste the sweetness, breath for breath. Keep the balance, death for death."
—Barrow witch incantation
Every day the cat returns to kill the same mouse, which sinks again into the cauldron's brew.
The dragon had a lot of things going through his mind that day. He didn't expect a sword to be one of them.

"I have seen things that would reduce a weaker person to blubbering and raving. Want to hear about them?"
—Vraska
"Wait, are *we* the decoys?"
"The penalty for idleness is death. The penalty for disputing the penalty is death."

"They exist only so long as the living take no notice."
—Kifimbo, Shadow guildmage
In Urborg, few things are less permanent than death.
True power is achieved through blood and sweat. But mostly blood.

"So the vulture said to the griffin, 'You gonna eat that?'"
—Azeworai, "The Ugly Bird"
The goblins made an unruly pile with military precision.

"Fire's out. Should be safe now."
—Gnarltrunk
To the sorrow of all, its rage became focused on those who once stoked it.
It puts the "fur" in "fury."
Through failure we learn our finest lessons in humility.
The orcs' banner sends a clear message: "Stand against us and meet the same fate as the goblins."
Enthusiasm can be tempered in the furnace of the earth.

"It is not in me to tread lightly."
—Ryda, geomancer

"The efreet is a striding storm with a voice that crackles like fire."
—Qhattib, vizier of Amiqat
"I pass to you all we have ever been. Go forth and become all we never could."
For the first time in many years, Elspeth asked for help.

"I fear no army or beast, but only the morning fog. Our assault can survive everything else."
—Lord Hilneth
One thread connected all the travelers' stories: the ferocity of the mongoose.
"For us, a rope represents the ties that bind the kor. For you, it's more literal."
When does majestic become ominous?
"If you ever want to leave this forest, now's the time."
"Don't laugh. It works."
"My rule persists beyond death itself."
Boros soldiers are like a cache of bombs ready to explode, and the flame-kin light their fuses.

"Even if we dislodge them, I fear these lands will never again yield crops."
—Kimmick, vanguard knight

"If you work at sawing up carcasses, you notice how the joints fit, how the nerves are arrayed, and how the skin peels back."
—Ashnod, to Tawnos
It is like life and destiny: we think we know the story, but we have read only half the tale.
The toymaker frowned in bewilderment. None of his creations had ever sneezed before.

"If you must go out at night, bring a mob."
—Master of the Elgaud Cathars

"Find the dens of evil and flood them with light."
—Hulo, the Penitent Wanderer
A kithkin's worst enemy is solitude.

"I search for a vision of Zendikar that does not include the Eldrazi."
—Expedition journal entry
"No fact escapes me. Why do you think you can?"

"It's hard to hurt anyone when you're as transparent as your motives."
—Ertai, wizard adept
Giving little thought to their own defense, they carried the flag that united their army.
What a lonely agony, the memory of memories lost.
"You can't learn to enjoy life's amusements in the pages of books. You must seek them out in earnest."
Summoners of efreeti remember only the power of command, never the sting of regret.
"By thorn and by stone, we will fight to see the day when beauty returns to this world."

"The floor of the sea is paved with the shattered remnants of vessels that navigated its surface unwelcomed."
—Thassa, god of the sea
On Evos Isle, the swift and formidable aven enforce the will of the ruling sphinxes.

"Whatever Yawgmoth marks, dies. There is no escape."
—Tsabo Tavoc, Phyrexian general
"See the beauty in death: the clean white bones lying in the fertile soil and the brightly colored moonglove sprouting from the fell earth."
Ending her life won't end the infestation.

"Don't worry. I'm not going to deprive you of all your secrets. Just your most precious one."
—Liliana Vess

"Those without beauty are Lorwyn's greatest tumor. The winnowers have an unpleasant duty, but a necessary one."
—Eidren, perfect of Lys Alana
A cry of pain as it enters this world. A chorus of screams as it leaves.
The priests plead for your anguish and pray for your despair.
Zombies mourn for the living and celebrate those who will soon be given the gift of death.
The famed hunting hounds of House Cecani continue to prove the quality of their pedigree.
Even if the rain turned to blood, her thirst would not be slaked.

"Emrakul makes apparent those whom she has favored."
—Runo Stromkirk

"Impressive."
—Chandra Nalaar
With fewer patrols about, Kessig's roads have become prime hunting grounds.
"Keep your herons and shrews! You will find nothing in the moon, for the moon is a lie! It has told me so!"
"Madness can't touch a mind ignited by genius."
Paranoia has driven some Kessig communities to hunt down anything—and anyone—that travels through their woods.
"May the steel of your blade match the steel in your soul."
"Bloodsuckers, howlers, monsters from the beyond . . . it doesn't much matter. I won't have to face them alone."

"More rope may not be necessary."
—Kep, Lunarch inquisitor

"There is no saving this world, not anymore. But we shall be its bloody vengeance."
—Sorin Markov

"These fiends are slightly less tolerable than you."
"A sentiment that warms my heart, sister."

"Procedural misstep: provocation of geists for the purpose of yielding more energy can compromise containment units. Next action: clean up mess."
—Laboratory notes

"May knowledge be our sanctuary."
—Yora, academy researcher

"I've seen cathars riding to battle without a hint of fear. Perhaps that is its own sort of madness."
—Esler, Havengul mercenary
Not all minds touched by the Eldrazi turn to raging psychosis. Some simply withdraw from this world into memories of a better one.
"There is always more to give."
"Let the points of our lances lead the way."
The uncorrupted rallied under Thalia's leadership and Sigarda's banner.

"Improvisation is for those who failed to prepare."
—Jace Beleren

"There's no sense arguing with insanity."
—Levana, Midnight Duelist
"I'll see you soon, Subjects 25 and 26. I've got a good feeling this time!"
"At last! Proof that it's not all in my head!"
It keeps intruders out and experiments in.

"There are tides beyond those in the sea that are driven by Innistrad's silver moon. If you learn their patterns, you can channel them in fascinating ways."
—Tamiyo

"Nicely done, Jace. You always were good at disappearing acts."
—Liliana Vess
All around Emrakul, life re-formed in her image.
Some spirits cling to one person, feasting on the growing fear until a final moment of all-consuming terror.
Transformed at his own wedding, he promptly ate the banquet, the gifts, and the guests.
No self-respecting criminal has a basement with only one exit.

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Destroy target nonland permanent an opponent controls.
II — Search your library for a Forest card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.
III — Creatures you control gain deathtouch until end of turn.

faces.f: "Life is a pattern, not a material."
Even across the Edge, a dog is still a dog.
Older than the Eumidian seedships that populated Evendo.
Seyden's temperament didn't take well to the puca's magic. Nor did his face.
Noggles believe that they were the first race ever to walk Shadowmoor. They don't "steal." They just take back what's rightfully theirs.
Kithkin somnomancers enjoy the peaceful dreams wafting from their victims.

"I knew a creature carved from a dream of wild freedom. Any attempt to leash or exploit it failed, and at terrible cost."
—Ashling
"Better for a doun to lose its cenn than its springjacks."
Do the glowing trinkets show it the way home, or do they set a twisted path for someone else to follow?
Bogles are very tasty if you can get the skin off. It's getting a blade on them that's the problem.
Her poppets bring joy to the truly depraved.
The more the scarier.
It plucks away memories like choice bits of carrion.
They once sought to unite with the flame of transcendence. Now they seek only to extinguish the lights of others.
"It's not much for eating, but I think we can find somethin' to do with it."
Its wings disturb more than air.
The Extinguisher's curse lasted long after her departure.
Beauty is a seed, waiting to blossom under her capable hands.
Some beasts are born not of a mother, but of magic.
"Living scarecrows make a mockery of the natural order. Dead ones make fine hats."

"Only a knife left for a fortnight in the hollow of a ghastbark tree can inflict a wound so grave."
—Kithkin superstition
A gwyllion's favorite trap is the vanity mirror. A bewitched piece of glass traps the looker's soul and does away with the body.
A snap of fingers, a snap of teeth.
Bores ruin a party. Boars are party to ruin.

"Volrath is not the only one who can shape this world to serve him."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves

"Civilization is a conspiracy to disguise the mutilation of nature."
—Skyshroud elite creed
Secure in the embrace of wood, they want no part of Eladamri's war.
"In Barrin's name!" cried Lyna as Hanna's sword passed through her, "Ertai sends word that the portal is open—but not for long!"
War favors the informed.
In Rath, there are only so many souls to go around.

"Consider the fable of the greedy herder. As her flock grew, so did her weariness; she slept, and the sheep wandered off."
—Karn, silver golem
Hunger is like the sea: deep, endless, and unforgiving.
The wizard had it all—until she tried to use it.
Karn and Hanna stood over the recovered Legacy artifacts like loving parents over sleeping children.
A farewell to arms . . . and feet . . . and legs . . . .
The last thing to go through the mogg's mind was its teeth.

"If we cannot live proudly, we die so!"
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
Man versus nature is not a fair fight.
Most creatures grow out of their baby teeth, but sabertooth wyverns grow into theirs.
Once rejected by his pride, Ajani is now revered by countless leonin as a healer and, more importantly, a friend.

"Ah, the conquering hero returns! What trials did you face, little one?"
—Basri Ket
Despite their advanced intellect, some aven never quite shake their instinctive need to collect shiny baubles.
"Don't worry about where they're taking me. The more pressing question is, why aren't they taking you?"
Gnorl and Vurg knew all too well how much dragons liked to eat goblins, but they had a dream that could not be dampened: they were going to be the first goblins to eat a dragon.
Slibbo was tired of following Korvold's draconian library rules.

"Our state-of-the-art laboratories have been stripped of bothersome safety measures."
—Radula, Simic biomancer
"Rise, my liege! Rise, and blanket the world in eternal night!"
"He asked me if I wanted to come in for a bite to eat. Who am I to turn down a stranger's kindness?"
Norf would win the arm-wrestling contest this year, at any cost.
Either you pay for Krenko's "protection" or you pay to replace your stall. Either way, you pay.
Ikko hadn't intended to start a riot, but now that it was under way, he was having a lot of fun.

"The Mardu are like the gore swine. We are wild, hunt in packs, and rarely clean the blood from our blades."
—Vallash, Mardu warrior

"You were once Mardu, so your body and will are strong. Now we must train your mind."
—Houn, Jeskai elder
Dragonslayers learned to keep silent about their deeds after seeing the terrible vengeance wrought by Kolaghan and her brood.

"Take inspiration from your enemies, and make their strengths your own."
—Alesha, Who Smiles at Death
His beasts move the great siege towers of the Abzan across the endless sands.
After countless attacks on the Salt Road where it passes through the frozen tundra, the Abzan began to refer to the area as Atarka territory rather than Temur lands.

In a stunning act of diplomacy, Yasova Dragonclaw ceded a portion of Temur lands to the Sultai. Her clan protested until they saw she had given the Sultai the breeding grounds of the krushoks. They hadn't realized she had a sense of humor.
Perfectly suited for life in the Shifting Wastes, the krushok is well protected by its horn, its hide, and its temper.
Each bronze disk on its harness is an offering from a young Temur hunter, a sign of respect to the spirits of the wild.
First, whispers of ancient days. Then, visions of things to come.
The Temur see themselves as a pack, their bonds more primal than the Abzan's.
The energies of the Temur lands are readily unleashed upon intruders.
The invader hoped he could survive the beast's jaws and emerge through its rotting skin.

"No machinations, no puppet strings, no plots. Just pure, sweeping death."
—Tasigur, the Golden Fang
"Speak little. Do much."
By studying dragon anatomy, Jeskai monks have learned how to locate clusters of nerves that will incapacitate even the mightiest dragons.
Ugin's magic reaches beyond the dragons. The clans have adapted it for war.
"The one who conquers the mind is greater than the one who conquers the world."
"Before you can open your third eye, you must prove you can open the first two."
Boundaries drawn on maps or marked with stone have no meaning for the Mardu.
The defenses of the Abzan extend well beyond the walls of their fortresses.
The Mardu warrior was overjoyed when Tasigur set him free and granted him passage through the jungle. He failed to notice the Sultai leader's cruel smile.
He enjoys his work, for he sees only the worst Abzan criminals: those who betray their own kin.
Dragons of Silumgar's brood begin to digest their prey even before consuming it, letting their caustic breath do much of the work.
"Words have yet to halt an arrow."
"Greet death with sword in hand."
"I have no clan, but I still have purpose."
Anger can empower those who embrace it.
Tidal forces of the blood moon wrench and buckle the land, drawing monoliths of stone and soil toward the flaming orb.
"The spirits of the mythic ones ever circle their beloved keep, forbidding entry to all who come with the heavy tread of hate."
Dweldian magi don't enter the Realm of Thrones when they die. Instead their souls are drawn to great works of magic.

"Life cannot be created and then abandoned. It must be nurtured and fed so that it may express its ripened might."
—Freyalise
His roots reach deep, nurtured not by soil and rain, but by millennia of experience.
Battered and beaten by years of salt and claw, he never ceased to walk, and to seed. Only now, in this time of rebirth, do his seeds take root.
Some nature mages unknowingly took advantage of the temporal energies still swirling on Dominaria. What they mistook for healing magic was in fact the manipulation of time.
Some mages forsake their scrolls and libraries to learn at the feet of ancient trees and sacred stones.
She wished for gold, but not for the strength to carry it.

"No rest. No mercy. No matter what."
—Memorial inscription
The musical sound of its turning triggers the tumblers of revelation.

"Touch no tree, break no branch, and speak only the question you wish answered."
—Von Yomm, elder druid, to her initiates
Having conquered the Bastion of Suns, the Ota took its light for their own.
Within each empty skull, it seeks ways to preserve its own failing undeath.
In the stronghold's dungeons, the shadows hide in the vermin.
There are no soloists in the chorus of Selesnya.
From the seeds of faith, great forests grow.

"Diametrically opposing energies in self-sealed plasmodermic bubbles make great pets!"
—Trivaz, Izzet mage
Cast out of the Conclave generations ago, these elves found a home in the corrupted districts of the Golgari.
The Izzet quickly suspended their policy of lifetime guarantees.

"Let the rest of Ravnica sneer. One way or another, they all end up in the undercity."
—Jarad
To the Golgari, anything buried is treasure.

"All matter, animate or not, rots when exposed to time. We merely speed up the process."
—Ezoc, Golgari rot farmer

"First, you must fight among the rank and file. It is there I will discern your skills as a leader."
—Aurelia, to Gideon Jura
"The hard part isn't landing in the saddle. The hard part is leaping before you see it."
"Subtlety is for lawmages and spies."

"Imagine a thunderstorm that's also a tactical genius. That's him."
—Dars Gostok, Firefist captain
Though less well-known than its army of soldiers, the Boros Legion's mage-priests are as respected by the innocent as they are hated by the ghosts of the guilty.

"Yes, Boros tactics are unparalleled. But when your comrades are dying around you, inner strength must carry the day."
—Gideon Jura, to Aurelia
Held aloft by metabolized magic, trygons are ravenous for sources of mystic fuel.

"As peace should be—gentle yet unstoppable."
—Augustin IV

"Let him be an example to others who would default on their debts to us."
—"The Cozen," Orzhov assassin
One moment, conscious only of a sense of repose. The next moment, hearing the trudge of his own footsteps. He sighed and squinted into the glare ahead.
Devil-blades and dripping blood make music Rakdos never tires of hearing.
Long ago, birds of paradise littered the skies. Thanks to the city's sprawl, most now exist as pets of society's elite.

"The Gruul embrace all things poisonous and living in the cracks of society."
—Teysa Karlov
Those who regard the Gruul as savage simpletons underestimate the subtle power of their shamans.
Once the felidar has marked you as prey, there's no point in running.

"Dear brother, it's sweet that you have chosen to share your toys with Ludevic, but I too have found some new playmates."
—Ghoulcaller Gisa
"Come, my wild children. Let's give the interlopers a woodland welcome."
Her haunting tune drowns out the percussion of snapping masts.
"If you've never feasted on Zagoth terror-pig, I got the best price you'll find."

"All are not equal—neither in life nor after death. Bontu's favorites will stand highest in eternity."
—Senifet, vizier of Bontu

"For all I have lost, for all who have fallen, I will render you to dust."
—Jared Carthalion

"I don't need your mage-rings or your mana equations. I call, and the sea answers."
—Keyta, rebel hydromancer
"Eldrazi? Ha! Try walking through Zulaport at night with your pockets full. Now *that's* dangerous."

"Want to sink a ship? Blow a hole in the hull. Want to kill a regisaur? Same answer."
—Captain Brandis Thorn
Goblins journey to the sacrificial peaks in pairs so that the rare survivor might be able to relate the details of the other's grisly demise.
As patient and generous as life, as harsh and merciless as nature.

"It's the must-have gift for everyone on your list. Get one for yourself, too!"
—Chammi, curio vendor
Each time it is sent to find a safe haven, it takes longer to return.
When it awoke, it spawned nameless thousands to herald its arrival.
When it awoke, the mirrors of the world reflected only darkness.
When it awoke, it shattered the hillsides to make way for its passage.
When it awoke, the worms of the earth hissed in a chorus of beckoning.
Unlike most churches, at Orzhova it's best to pray before you arrive.
His assistants calculate the amount of the tribute. He measures out the punishment for delinquency.

"When you hear thunder on a cloudless day, take cover and brace for the coming of the storm herd."
—Skotov, Tin Street basket vendor

"The call came, spell-borne through mortar and stone to the ear of every soldier. The call came, and the advantage was ours."
—Lodusz, captain of the watch

"I watched its blade swing through me, but I was hollow, empty. I saw its face contort in rage but could not hear it snarl."
—Klattic, Boros legionnaire
"Rauck-Chauv's like a holiday! Only it isn't on the calendars, and instead of dancing you knock people flat, and instead of giving gifts you break stuff."
"Watch carefully. The gap between death and victory is thinner than your blade."

"He's got more finesse than most goblins. He smashes windows with his fist rather than his forehead."
—Arrester Polgar

"Commander, we caught the Dimir spy and took her ashes into custody."
—Kramm, Wojek security officer
"I packed three more electroconduits into each test wand. You'll experience a brief tingling sensation."
"Light a torch and deliver this letter" were his instructions, which he unfortunately reversed.
"By all means, take another step toward the captain."
The problem isn't the indrik's enthusiasm, it's Ravnica's lack of guardrails.
"The tiniest mouse speaks louder to me than all the festival crowds on Tin Street."

"The shortest path between two points is not always the safest."
—Tamina, district guide

"The Dimir may look all they want. We never grow tired of swatting their bugs."
—Heruj, Selesnya hierophant

Feed on food, you eventually rot. Feed on rot, you live forever.
—Kraul saying
Selesnya grows its ranks in more ways than one.
The wounded see the glow of its vials long before they see its wings diving out of the clouds.

"Light up the dark to find your way, and the dark may seek you out."
—Zalin the Gutter Bard
Suddenly, all the haggling didn't seem so important.
"Send your champion. I could use a light workout."

"Within the song of Mat'Selesnya, one becomes all."
—Heruj, Selesnya hierophant
"Whatever hatred destroys, a single act of trust can revive."
Good at carrying things. Really good at knocking them down.
Giants know a solid hit is one part strength, four parts leverage.

"It's like blowing up an arcane library in a thermobaric explosion. But in a good way."
—Bori Andon, Izzet blastseeker
"We are the shield that never breaks, the bough that never burns, the song that can never be silenced."
"The dagger is just a distraction. I carry the real killer in a vial at my side."
"I long for peaceful times, when I may tend to my garden instead of our borders."
"It's truly the highest honor, isn't it? To be remembered? Pity for you."

"Something's causing electrospheric disruption in the blazekite's spire-vanes. Find the cause, and tell them to keep it up!"
—Juzba, Izzet tinker
By guild tradition, any puddle of multicolored light on the cobblestones can serve as neutral ground.

"The more trust breaks down, the more we must throw open the front gates."
—Aurelia

"Every guild dreads infiltration. I should know—I've been a member of all of them."
—Lazav
The Chamber of the Guildpact stands as a reminder that even the bitterest struggles can end in cooperation.

"Shut the gates. In the Underrealm we will outlast the coming doom."
—Vraska
Every laboratory buzzes with new experiments, each a piece of Ral's ambitious project.

"Everyone who crosses that threshold is our most cherished friend. Everyone who crosses it again is our bitterest enemy."
—Trostani
Selesnya guildmages do not sleep so the rest of the conclave can.
"My specialty is theoretical universal limits and ways to circumvent them."
All those who trade in questions must answer to the Dimir.

"Most compete for insects at street level. Some dwell near Izzet laboratories and ride the thermal updrafts."
—Yolov, Simic bioengineer
Rumors float through the city like crows, alighting on citizens seemingly at random.

"Reports of Gruul rioters in four districts. Start with the big ones and work your way up."
—Libuse, Boros sergeant
"There's no need to sound the alarm. You are minding your post admirably. I am authorized. All is well."

"What wishes do they grant? Mostly pinching-related ones."
—Omik, superintendent of waterworks

"Bats are welcome to eat thousands of my pets. I have multitudes more that will ultimately eat the bats."
—Izoni
All things considered, his first day on patrol could have gone better.
Ravnica's safest strongholds are often neither.

"To wage war, secure peace within yourself."
—Emmara
Dimir assassins have the precision to slay a single memory.
"My power is generosity, in a way. I give my survivors an appreciation for their lives."
"I've seen Ravnica's fate. Believe me, I'm doing you a favor."
"Don't stop till your horns come out their back."
"This sort of innovation occurs when you set out to improve an electric tea kettle and misplace a decimal."

"It's both an ingress-denial mechanism and an attractive hallway light!"
—Daxiver, Izzet electromancer
The most nimble of creatures, it chases the most sacred luminence.
It is said that Yinglong gave birth to the qilin and the phoenix, and after them, all the hairy and winged beings in the world. Thus it is known as the Ancestor Dragon.
Mystery lies beneath the haunting mists. Never stay where obscurity deepens.

"The Ancestor Dragon appeared atop the clouds, amid shattering mountains and sundering earth."
—Jiang Yanggu's travelogue
A heaven-sent vision is like a lantern to guide the way.
This strange beast has the hide of a leopard, the howl of a dog, and the horns of an ox.
Known for their glowing horn and stone-rattling roar, zheng are the fiercest predators in the forest. Few survived before Jiang Yanggu came.
A precious shell without, a delicious taste within.

"Mowu was wary that day, as though he sensed the danger ahead."
—Jiang Yanggu's travelogue
"Crackle" and "pop" are the most wondrous sounds.
It stops flying only as its life comes to an end.
It has waited a millennium just for you, and for a millennium will it watch over your descendants.
Scream: muffled. Pockets: emptied. Neck function: never the same again.
He tired of his fellow researchers and their useless prattling, so he decided to make a network of scholars with whom he could carry a conversation.

"Debt and death sound so similar, and thrulls are so hard of hearing. Mistakes are inevitable."
—Milana, Orzhov prelate

"A regression to ancient forms? A glimpse of future evolutions? Or a fleeting alteration of the present?"
—Vorel of the Hull Clade
It's easy to believe you're a god when you're twice as powerful as everyone else.
Amid rumors of war, the third act of *The Absolution of the Guildpact* was quickly rewritten as a tragedy.

"Entrance is free. Donations are required."
—Notice outside Vizkopa Bank
The hunger of a vampire and the subtlety of a tax collector.
"Scandal and slander are never welcome news. That's why I'm never the messenger."

"Finding a true heartstone is even harder than finding a true heart."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator
A few coins soon grow into an obsession.

"All memory of your existence will be wiped from reality. You will die, and no one will mourn."
—Memnarch
All Auriok children know the tale, "Bolgri and the Long Day of Squashing."
As the fifth sun joins the other four, new abilities awaken in the creatures of Mirrodin.
Shadowmoor's main crops are rot, slime, and despair.
Left to itself, nature overflows any container, overthrows any restriction, and overreaches any boundary.

"When the wielder is strong enough, any sword will do."
—Kresh the Bloodbraided
"There is no tomorrow, so hold nothing back."

"I was promised an afterlife, not this. Samut was right. The God-Pharaoh lied."
—Djeru, former Tah-crop initiate
Though buried and muffled, nature's whisper still called to Nissa.

"Remember, brother, the eyes are always vulnerable."
"I never forgot."
Once favored companions, many cats were left to fend for themselves.
"This is the final trial! Rejoice, for the God-Pharaoh soars among us!"

"It's a cruel thing to give such a sad song to such a colorful creature."
—Sana, former Ahn-crop initiate
Decades to build. Hours to demolish.
"What will happen to us?" they asked. The vizier paused. "I think . . . I think that's up to us now."
The God-Pharaoh's most devoted took it upon themselves to follow his example.

"Bolas remade this place in his image. He has the advantage here. We must approach carefully."
—Jace Beleren
The denizens of the Luxa River woke angry on the currents of blood.

"It is evidence that some pure corner of the world must still exist."
—Djeru, former Tah-crop initiate
Initiates once believed defeat was the worst fate possible—a sentiment they quickly abandoned.
With the Hekma destroyed, the wandering dead that sought entrance to Naktamun had free rein to lay waste to the city.
From every shadow came the dull scratch of teeth on bones.
Yell for help, and that may answer.
"Your God-Pharaoh has returned."
The Scorpion God's sting sends venom strong enough to poison blood, bone, and spirit.
Samut battled her way through the hordes, shouting the names of those who'd died in her crop and those she hoped yet to save.
Without the viziers to oversee their actions, some anointed went to extreme lengths to fulfill their directives.
A word of vengeance, and her arrows awaken in flame.
The God-Pharaoh's benevolence concealed the factory he created to produce an army of Eternals.

"That one's not mine. Run!"
—Nissa Revane
"When the whole world is crazy, it's important to find something you can rely on."
